boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Springfield (Zagonyi's Charge) record (October 25, 1861) in Operations to Control Missouri [June-October 1861]. Fremont's advance from the Osage and his occupation of Springfield on October 27 are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the Prairie Scouts and Fremont's Body Guard and State Guard troops with no figures; the live field reads zero; NPS gives Frazier 1,000 to 1,500. Zagonyi says his Body Guard numbered 150, rallied to 70 after the charges, and that White's command left him before the first charge; he learned afterwards that 2,100 of the enemy had been arrayed. Britton gives Zagonyi 150 and White 180 mounted men, and at least 1,500 Confederates in town, outnumbering them five to one.
claims.rationale: Detachment counts and after-the-fact estimates of the enemy; no return. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Colonel James Frazier and Major James Zagonyi; the live page gives Zagonyi as Major General, and its description names Maj. Charles Zagonyi and Col. Julian Frazier. NPS says White fell ill and turned his command over to Zagonyi; Zagonyi says White was a prisoner before the battle and his command left at the start; Britton says Zagonyi and White together decided the detour.
claims.rationale: The detachment commanders' roles are disputed among the sources; the live ranks and names are not adopted, and there is no automatic sole credit.

claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text and the live field read 218 (US 85; CS 133). Zagonyi reports a total loss of 52 in the Body Guard (15 killed), at least 106 enemy killed by citizens' and prisoners' statements, 23 enemy dead buried and 27 prisoners; Britton gives sixteen Federal killed and twenty-six wounded.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Zagonyi's total covers the Body Guard only.

open_questions: Fremont's No. 1 report and inclosures, White's account, Naughton's No. 3 report (printed after Zagonyi's; glanced while delimiting the selection, not selected), the State Guard side, returns and maps remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, vol. I (second edition, 1891) is a retrospective history by a Union soldier of the border army, based by its title page on the official reports; it is not independent of the report families. Zagonyi's October 28, 1861 report is an interested Union account. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
